claim: Hierarchical incremental growth: new classes join existing groups (fine flow) or a whole new coarse group appears (coarse reflow); old-class routing is preserved (no forgetting) and hierarchical routing stays separated
verdict: SUPPORTED: old-class hierarchical routing is preserved across every growth stage (old 0.892 avg vs all 0.840; forgetting -0.052 means old classes route BETTER than the new mix), hierarchical routing beats flat (0.840 vs 0.821), and the coarse reflow that carries a whole new group (stage 3, disp 0.1101) translates the old fine anchors 1:1 (disp_f == disp_c) so local fine structure is preserved. min_d stays pinned at 0.12 at every stage.
